# Assembly guide: printer_v9

Generated by `tools/build_package.py` from `designs/printer_v9.py` (md5 `6db7a4c15ad561e4616084adc1fcfba4`) and `out/printer_v9/report.json` (written 2026-11-18 09:16:36, md5 `06c8e34614ad`). Do not edit: change the design, re-run verify, re-run the generator.

> **Simulated design. Nothing has been built.** See [OPEN_ITEMS.md](OPEN_ITEMS.md) before spending money.

584 parts, 195 drawn screws (20 types), tools: 2 mm hex key, 2.5 mm hex key, 3 mm hex key, 4 mm hex key. The simulation's time allowance is 138.1 min: a figure for comparing designs. It does not contain the operations listed under 'Not in the simulation' below, which are a large part of the real work.

## Read this first: what this guide is and is not

- **Bench units** below follow the assembly simulation step for step (it found an order with a way in for every part and driver access for every screw).
- **The main assembly does NOT follow the simulation's order.** That order is valid for access but is not one a person can build: 3 of its steps place a unit before anything supports it (it fits the bed carrier at step ? and the frame's posts at steps 396 to 398, the corner brackets last), it turns the machine over 14 times and does 20 operations from below. The cause is in the model: corner brackets on T-slots have no drawn screws, so nothing 'holds' the frame until the end. The stages below re-group the simulation's units into the order a builder uses (frame first). **That stage order has not been run through the access checker.** Each screw's driving direction is given in machine axes so access can be judged before a part is fitted over it. The simulation's own sequence is in `data/assembly_plan.json` and `data/assembly_simulated_order.md`.
- Torque: neither the parts catalogue nor the joint model holds a tightening torque for any screw. Every 'snug' below is the builder's judgement. Printed parts and circuit boards: do not crush.
- Washers: the model has none. See OPEN_ITEMS.md (washer audit) and decide before you start; a washer under a head changes how far the screw reaches (thread engagement was checked without them).
- Directions: front is -Y (the side the bed plate overhangs), right is +X, up is +Z.

![overall](images/overall_views.png)

## Not in the simulation (do these; they are not in the step lists or the time)

- 123 M5 and 32 M3 T-nuts: one under every screw marked 'into T-nut' and under every corner-bracket leg on a slot.
- 64 M5 x 8 corner-bracket screws on T-slots (32 brackets): counted in the BOM, not drawn, so not in any step.
- Tapping M5 in the extrusion ends listed in BOM.md (cut lengths, end work).
- Pulley set screws (all pulleys), the nyloc nut under each lead-screw nut's pin (leave 0.2 mm slack so the nut can float), the star washer under the earth stud.
- Bonding the heater pad, the thermal cut-off and the magnetic sheet to the plate. Fit the four bed posts and their jam nuts BEFORE the magnetic sheet: it covers their heads.
- Belts: X and Y (thread, fold back in the anchors, tie); the closed Z belt must be laid round the three screw pulleys, the idler and the motor pulley BEFORE the bed carrier is lowered onto the lead-screw nuts (afterwards the carrier is in the way).
- All wiring (WIRING.md), looms, cable ties, the BAT85 diode in the probe lead.
- Deburring every cut and machined part (the model has sharp edges everywhere).

Three uprights (v9): one in the left wall and one in the right wall at y -32, one in the back wall at x 65, each between a bottom and a top rail on two cast brackets per end. Slide each ZF block onto its rail before the rail goes on its upright. Rail alignment: see 'rail_align (z)' below: the rear rail is set square to the frame; the left and right rails are tightened last, with the carrier bolted to all three blocks and run up and down, so each rail takes the position the carrier gives it.
Use clearance-class (ZF) blocks on Z: the three screws hold the carrier's tilt, the blocks only locate it.

Cut each lead-screw motor's screw to 258 mm above the motor face (hacksaw, file a 0.5 mm chamfer, run the nut over the cut end) before fitting. Each motor is a bench unit: motor under its plate (the three plates are one shape), pilot in the plate's 22.3 mm hole, four M3 x 10 from above with medium thread locker (they reach 3.65 mm into the motor's 4.5 mm threads: do not substitute longer screws). Stand the two spacers on the rail (rear) or the tray over the rail (front), the unit on them, the M5 x 70 post bolts with washers into the T-nuts, thread locker. The screw must turn freely by hand, and its top end is free: no bearing.

Build the carrier upside down on a flat table (the deck's top face down): lay the deck, set the four 2020 members on it, a cast bracket in each inside corner on T-nuts in both legs, then the ten deck bolts from the deck side, thread locker. Check the diagonals. Bolt the three carriage plates to the members' outer faces (two M5 each) and the three nut plates under the members (two M5 each). The order differs from the simulation's, which builds part by part in the machine.
Each T8 nut: flange under its plate, barrel up through the float hole, pin (M2.5 through the 5 mm sleeve, nylon-insert nut), then the keeper under the flange on its two M3 bolts and 3.6 mm spacers (0.1 mm play: the nut must slide sideways by hand).
Turn the three motors by hand until the nuts sit at the same height, lower the carrier onto the screws, and screw each carriage plate to its block (four M3 x 5 with washers and thread locker: they reach 2.9 mm into the block's 3.5 mm threads, do not substitute longer screws). Do not force a plate onto its block: slacken the rail instead. Check: the carrier runs the full travel without binding; then Z_TILT_ADJUST.

No tapping in the bed plate. Countersink the four holes from the top face if SendCutSend did not (90 degrees to 8.96 mm for M4). Then, plate upside down on the bench: each M4 x 35 FULLY THREADED countersunk screw through from the top face, washer and nut under the plate with medium thread locker, tightened against the countersink (the screw is now a fixed stud); heater pad and thermal cut-off bonded under the plate between the studs.
Springs over the four studs, an M4 washer on each spring. Lower the plate so the studs pass the deck's four holes (stud 0, front left, has the fitted hole; front right the slot). From below: large M4 washer and thumb nut on each stud. Run every thumb nut up until its spring is 14 mm long (plate underside 18.8 mm above the deck), then level (adjustment section). THEN the magnetic base and the print sheet.

## Alignment and adjustment

Every `Adjustment` the design declares, with what the tolerance simulation says it must absorb (99th percentile of the simulated builds) against what the design provides.

### z_offset: probe z_offset in the firmware

- Needed 1.08 mm (99 %); provided 1.65 mm of Z over-travel past the nominal nozzle plane.
- **Probe height (on its two nuts):** sensing face 2.0 mm above the nozzle tip as drawn. It must stay inside the face window **[0.56, 3.44] mm** above the tip (lower: the face could meet the bed before the nozzle, margin 0.56 mm; upper: the weakest sensor would not switch in time). Set it with a 2.0 mm gauge block (or stacked feeler gauges) under the face while the cold nozzle rests on the bare print sheet; tighten both nuts; re-measure.
- Then `PROBE_CALIBRATE`: predicted z_offset 3.0 mm, anywhere in [2.0, 4.0] mm over sensor spread and temperature ([2.5, 3.5] mm over unit spread alone). These figures assume the sensor reads the thin spring-steel sheet like OMRON's iron target: UNVERIFIED, see COMMISSIONING.md step B1.
- Check: PROBE_ACCURACY passes the configured `samples_tolerance`; the nozzle touches paper at Z = 0 with the bed at working temperature.

### bed_level: the knurled thumb nut under the deck at each of the four bed studs (0.7 mm per turn)

- Needed 0.72 mm (99 %); provided +/-2 mm of thread at each post. As built, before tramming, the bed is up to 1.45 mm out of level (99 %).
- How: at each of the four posts the plate's height is set by the nut above the tab and locked by the nut below it. Home X and Y, bring the nozzle over each post position in turn, and set each corner to the same feeler-gauge gap under the cold nozzle (or zero a dial indicator clamped to the toolhead). Go round twice. Lock each lower nut while holding the upper one with a second spanner.
- Check: all four corners within 0.1 mm of each other (half a 0.2 mm layer, the report's own criterion) after locking; re-check after the first heat cycle to working temperature. The posts' jam nuts under the plate must be tight before the magnetic sheet goes on.

### endstop (x): x switch: its screws run in slots in the Y plate's land

- Switch x_endstop, struck by x_carriage, at the min end. Working end of travel -90.0 mm, mechanical end -91.5 mm (joint coordinates).
- Needed: 0.6 mm (99 %); provided: +/-2 mm. As drawn, without setting, 42% of builds miss the window ([-0.1, 0.23] mm wide around the drawn position).
- How: with the switch's screws nipped, move the axis by hand to its mechanical end (against whatever stops it). Slide the switch towards the striker until it has clicked and the lever is still clear of the switch body, then back it off so the click happens between 0 and 3.0 mm before the end. Tighten.
- Check: the click is heard before the end of travel from a slow hand approach, three times; at the mechanical end the lever is not crushed on the case (the maker guarantees only 0.55 mm of lever travel past the click; case contact is 0.25 mm past the latest operating position). The axis must be stopped by the signal, never by the switch.

### endstop (y): y switch: its mount slides along the rail on two T-nuts

- Switch y_endstop, struck by y_plate_right, at the max end. Working end of travel 107.25 mm, mechanical end 108.75 mm (joint coordinates).
- Needed: 1.49 mm (99 %); provided: +/-5 mm. As drawn, without setting, 75% of builds miss the window ([-0.1, 0.23] mm wide around the drawn position).
- How: with the switch's screws nipped, move the axis by hand to its mechanical end (against whatever stops it). Slide the switch towards the striker until it has clicked and the lever is still clear of the switch body, then back it off so the click happens between 0 and 3.0 mm before the end. Tighten.
- Check: the click is heard before the end of travel from a slow hand approach, three times; at the mechanical end the lever is not crushed on the case (the maker guarantees only 0.55 mm of lever travel past the click; case contact is 0.25 mm past the latest operating position). The axis must be stopped by the signal, never by the switch.

### rail_align (y): y rails on sliding T-nuts

Design note: an M3 in the 6.2 mm slot slides +/-1.6 mm: left rail to a straight edge, right rail tightened while the gantry runs.

- Rails: y_rail_left, y_rail_right. As built, before alignment: out of parallel by up to 1.284 mm over the travel (99 %). Allowed by the maker: 0.009 mm (Hiwin MG catalogue Table 3.88 (p.104): MG_12, preload Z0). Share of builds inside that without alignment: 0.0. Adjustment provided: +/-1.6 mm (T-nuts sliding across the slot). **The machine depends on this step.**
- How: tighten the first rail against a straight edge (Y) or a square off the bottom rail (Z). Leave the second rail's screws nipped. Fit what joins the two blocks (the gantry beam; the bed carrier's back plate), run it to one end, tighten the second rail's screws nearest the block, run to the other end, tighten there, then the screws between, moving the block to each screw.
- Check: by hand the axis moves over its whole travel with the same light drag everywhere and no tight end. The maker's 0.009 mm cannot be measured with shop tools; drag is the test. The simulation's un-aligned case would add 96.3 N of drag.

### rail_align (z): z rails on sliding T-nuts

Design note: rear rail to a square; left and right rails tightened while the carrier is run up and down; what is left goes into the carriage plates' webs.

- Rails: z_rail_left, z_rail_right, z_rail_rear. As built, before alignment: out of parallel by up to 1.094 mm over the travel (99 %). Allowed by the maker: 0.009 mm (Hiwin MG catalogue Table 3.88 (p.104): MG_12, preload ZF). Share of builds inside that without alignment: 0.191. Adjustment provided: +/-1.6 mm (T-nuts sliding across the slot). **The machine depends on this step.**
- How: tighten the first rail against a straight edge (Y) or a square off the bottom rail (Z). Leave the second rail's screws nipped. Fit what joins the two blocks (the gantry beam; the bed carrier's back plate), run it to one end, tighten the second rail's screws nearest the block, run to the other end, tighten there, then the screws between, moving the block to each screw.
- Check: by hand the axis moves over its whole travel with the same light drag everywhere and no tight end. The maker's 0.009 mm cannot be measured with shop tools; drag is the test. The simulation's un-aligned case would add 6.15 N of drag.

### float (z): floating lead screw nut

- Each lead-screw nut hangs under its printed block with +/-2.6 mm of radial room; a pin in a slot stops it turning. Needed: up to 2.54 mm (99 %, worst screw: leadscrew 2.54, leadscrew_fl 2.34, leadscrew_fr 2.25). Margin 0.06 mm.
- How: nothing to set, but it must be true: the nyloc nut under each pin is left 0.2 mm slack; the nut's flange is not clamped.
- Check: with the bed at the bottom, the middle and the top of its travel, each nut can still be pushed sideways a little in its pocket in every direction. A nut hard against one side of its pocket at either end of the travel has used all its float: re-seat that screw's pedestal or mount.

### belt_tension (x): x belt: idler plate slides on its T-nuts, pushed by an M3 jack screw in a PEM nut

- x_belt (9 mm): **14.2 N per span** is what the motor shaft-load check used (Gates' minimum installation tension for the width; Gates' 'general' figure is 75.6 N). Tensioner travel +/-3 mm.
  - Measure by plucking a free span at the home position and reading the pitch (phone tuner app): 104.0 mm span: about 189 Hz; 236.0 mm span: about 83 Hz; 104.0 mm span: about 189 Hz. From f = sqrt(T / mu) / 2L with mu = 9.2 g/m, a figure the catalogue DERIVES from Gates' constants (not printed by Gates): treat +/-10 %.
  - Spans at home: [104.0, 236.0, 104.0] mm.
- Check: after 20 full strokes the pitch has not dropped.

### belt_tension (y): y belts: motor mounts slide on their T-nuts, pushed by M3 jack screws in PEM nuts

- y_belt (12 mm): **18.7 N per span** is what the motor shaft-load check used (Gates' minimum installation tension for the width; Gates' 'general' figure is 106.8 N). Tensioner travel +/-3 mm.
  - Measure by plucking a free span at the home position and reading the pitch (phone tuner app): 124.0 mm span: about 159 Hz; 388.9 mm span: about 51 Hz; 229.5 mm span: about 86 Hz. From f = sqrt(T / mu) / 2L with mu = 12.1 g/m, a figure the catalogue DERIVES from Gates' constants (not printed by Gates): treat +/-10 %.
  - Spans at home: [124.0, 388.9, 229.5] mm.
- y_belt_l (12 mm): **18.7 N per span** is what the motor shaft-load check used (Gates' minimum installation tension for the width; Gates' 'general' figure is 106.8 N). Tensioner travel +/-3 mm.
  - Measure by plucking a free span at the home position and reading the pitch (phone tuner app): 124.0 mm span: about 159 Hz; 388.9 mm span: about 51 Hz; 229.5 mm span: about 86 Hz. From f = sqrt(T / mu) / 2L with mu = 12.1 g/m, a figure the catalogue DERIVES from Gates' constants (not printed by Gates): treat +/-10 %.
  - Spans at home: [124.0, 388.9, 229.5] mm.
- Check: both Y belts read the same pitch on the same span (the gantry must not rack); after 20 full strokes the pitch has not dropped.
